title: Lakeflow Designer Summer Release
body:
The Lakeflow Designer Summer Release adds new operators, expands the Output and Join operators, and improves the canvas editing experience. The following updates are now available:

* **Prepare operator**: Use the new Prepare operator for common data-cleansing tasks, including changing text case and data types, replacing values, and applying formulas. See [Prepare](/aws/en/designer/built-in-operators#prepare).
* **Enter Data operator**: Manually create tabular data in a spreadsheet-style editor. See [Enter Data](/aws/en/designer/built-in-operators#enter-data).
* **Select operator**: Use the new Select operator to choose which columns to keep, rename columns, and reorder them in the output. See [Select](/aws/en/designer/built-in-operators#select).
* **Visualization operator**: Create and view visualizations directly on the canvas. See [Visualization](/aws/en/designer/built-in-operators#visualization).
* **Improved Output operator**: The Output operator now supports inserting or appending data in Unity Catalog tables, publishing results as materialized views, and writing CSV, Excel, or JSON files to Unity Catalog volumes. See [Output](/aws/en/designer/built-in-operators#output).
* **Split Join outputs**: The Join operator now provides three outputs by default: unmatched left rows, matched rows, and unmatched right rows. This makes it easier to branch a workflow based on join results. See [Join](/aws/en/designer/built-in-operators#join).
* **Case-sensitive joins**: The Join operator now includes a **Match case** option and matches string keys case-insensitively by default.
* **Matched and unmatched Filter outputs**: The Filter operator now provides separate outputs for matching and non-matching rows, so you can branch data based on whether it meets the filter conditions. See [Filter](/aws/en/designer/built-in-operators#filter).
* **Improved date filtering**: The Filter operator's date picker now supports navigating across years as well as months.
* **Additional AI functions**: The AI Function operator now supports `ai_query`, `ai_parse_document`, `ai_forecast`, and `ai_prep_search`. See [AI Function](/aws/en/designer/built-in-operators#ai-function).
* **Folder and volume inputs**: The Source operator can now target an entire Unity Catalog volume or folder path instead of an individual file. See [Source](/aws/en/designer/built-in-operators#source).
* **Metric view sources**: Use Unity Catalog metric views as source nodes in Lakeflow Designer. See [Source](/aws/en/designer/built-in-operators#source).
* **Inline Note editing**: The Note operator now supports inline rich-text editing directly on the canvas, including headings, text styling, links, images, and tables. See [Note](/aws/en/designer/built-in-operators#note).
* **Easier node connections**: Redesigned node ports provide larger connection targets and clearer visual cues, making operators easier to connect.
* **Clearer operator configuration cues**: Unconfigured operators now have a dashed border, and required input ports that aren't connected are highlighted in yellow.
* **Table of contents panel**: Find and navigate to any operator using the new searchable table of contents in the left sidebar. Select an operator to focus it on the canvas, then expand the **Generated code** section to view its underlying code.
* **Command palette**: Press Cmd+Shift+P on macOS or Ctrl+Shift+P on Windows to quickly access editor actions.
* **Visual data prep listing page**: Find all of your visual data prep files from a dedicated **Visual data prep** page in the sidebar. The page includes a getting-started video banner to help you start using Lakeflow Designer.
* **Improved caching**: On all-purpose compute, downstream operators can reuse cached upstream results, reducing repeated work for long-running steps such as AI functions.
* **Large-canvas performance**: Scrolling and panning are more responsive on canvases with more than 200 operators.
* **Serverless environment selection**: When working with visual data prep files, you can now choose the serverless environment used for both interactive runs and scheduled jobs.
* **Improved scheduled-job readability**: Scheduled visual data prep runs now display each operator as an individual node in the Jobs task graph instead of showing raw Python code.
* **Declarative Automation Bundles support**: Deploy and run visual data prep files with Declarative Automation Bundles by configuring them as notebook tasks and referencing the file path in `notebook_task.notebook_path`. See [Move a visual data prep file to production](/aws/en/designer/production).
